correctness.rationale: Every quantifier is finite q>=2, all real y, beta<=1 globally, beta>1 sufficiently close to one for exactly two; beta>1 all values for existence. Gaussian quadrature exactness follows from Hermite orthogonality; positivity of weights from squared Lagrange cardinal polynomials. Hermite interpolation of e^{yt} has nonnegative 2q-th order remainder for both signs of y and strict positive Gaussian integral off the nodes. Orthogonal norm q! yields the exact first unmatched moment and Taylor coefficient. Bernoulli entropy reduction and quadratic supremum are identities over all invariant measures, not approximations. Coercivity and strict global gap localize maximizers before local analytic uniqueness is used. The polynomial square obstruction and parity of He_q prove minimal support and equality rigidity. Standalone NumPy script passed 128 finite diagnostics, supporting but not replacing the analytic proof. No claim of all-beta uniqueness or external certification.

value.rationale: The 2026 Taylor criterion leaves open a concrete model-design question: can every higher critical exponent be realized on a full finite-state shift without precritical phases, and how many symbols are necessary? This theorem supplies a uniform positive-weight construction, a strict all-field global threshold bound, exact onset and pressure constants, and a sharp minimal-alphabet/rigidity classification. The q=4 four-state sixth-root case is the first higher-order example beyond square-root/tricritical examples, and all q follow. These facts are motivated structural laws, not routine finite enumeration or an arbitrary slice; generic nonlinear pressure duality alone cannot answer the optimal alphabet question.
